audit_after: BOTH levers, and not between them, DECLARED BEFORE EITHER IS APPLIED. They are one pass because the first decides WHICH NUMBER the second compares against a price: the study currently publishes a median across two framings, so re-striking it on the latest price would audit the gap of a number [R-LENS-03] is about to retire. A look taken between them would audit a state this study never publishes. THE SIZE IS KNOWN IN ADVANCE AND IS THE REASON FOR DECLARING IT HERE: the first lever moves the answer from 1.4770 to somewhere between 2.3481 and 2.5499, +59% to +73%, which would carry this study from 38% BELOW its price to roughly at or above it — across [R-GAP-02]'s publication block in the direction that RELEASES it. That is precisely the shape where a rebuild must be decided on the rules rather than on where it lands, and the choice between the two framings is made below on the rules alone.

levers.name: the nine-reading median retired for the class primary, published two-sided
levers.why: the delivered central was the MEDIAN of nine readings spanning two costs of capital and two answers to the crux, which is a blend at equal weights nobody chose and nobody tested. Two defects rode inside it and each is worth more than the other. (i) FIVE of the nine were struck on a SECTOR bottom-up beta the study itself does not adopt — its own committed beta record carries a conforming tier-1 own-stock regression against the exchange index, so the median was half built on a cost of capital this study rejects, and every one of those five sits below every one of the four on the adopted beta. (ii) The remaining spread is the CRUX — whether navigation through the Strait of Hormuz is restored during 2026 — and a median across a question with two answers publishes a number true under neither. [R-LENS-03] settles both: ONE class primary is the central, the other lenses are cross-checks published beside it, and where the answer turns on a judgement the reader is shown the judgement. The cash-flow lens on the adopted beta is the primary for this class; the book-value and relative-multiple reads stay as cross-checks; the normalised-earnings read and every sector-beta read come out of the answer entirely.
levers.evidence: at the delivered spot the two branches on the adopted beta are AED 2.5499 if navigation normalises and AED 2.3481 if the disruption persists, against the retired median of AED 1.4770; the branch-to-branch spread is AED 0.2018 per share, and the median sat BELOW BOTH of them because the five sector-beta readings dragged it there. Both branches are carried in study_numbers.json under central_two_sided with the condition each one holds under, and the retired median is published beside them as what it was.

levers.name: the answer re-struck on the latest known price
levers.why: the study was struck against a close of AED 2.40 from 7 August 2026 and delivered against it a month later. [R-GAP-01] requires the central to be put against the LATEST KNOWN price before any delivery, and the price it publishes to be that same price with its date. The spot is not a decoration here: market-value equity weights are what [R-COC-01] requires, so the close feeds the capital structure and therefore the discount rate and therefore the answer. This lever moves the value only through that route — no driver, no path and no lens changed with it.
levers.evidence: AED 2.35 at 3 September 2026, from the supplied close register. A lower close lowers the market value of equity, raises the debt weight and therefore lowers the cost of capital, which raises the value: the persistent branch moves 2.3481 to 2.3524 and the normalisation branch 2.5499 to 2.5543, +0.18% and +0.17%. Both branches now sit at or above the price (+0.1% and +8.7%), which is the side of [R-GAP-02] that releases rather than holds — and the release was not the reason for either lever, which is why the audit point was declared before the first one was touched.

note: Several levers serving ONE rule are one piece of evidence, not several. `rules` combines them; `levers` keeps the order they were applied in so the route can be walked.

branches.why: [R-GAP-02] holds a two-sided answer only if EVERY branch breaches, so the low branch is the one that must clear the block on its own. Walking it cannot flatter the rebuild.
